title: Writing a Spatial Data Science Project

questions.prompt: A list of every county's median house value, with no summary or map, is:
questions.explain: Raw values without context are data.

questions.prompt: A map showing which counties have the highest house values is:
questions.explain: Data organized and summarized become information.

questions.prompt: You can have information without data.
questions.explain: You can have data without information, but not information without data.

questions.prompt: Which level sits at the top of the DIKW pyramid?
questions.explain: Data, information, knowledge, wisdom.

questions.prompt: Put the levels of the DIKW pyramid in order, from bottom to top.
questions.explain: Each level builds on the one below.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of the data science workflow in order.
questions.explain: Transform, visualize, and model repeat until you understand the data.

questions.prompt: The three Vs of big data are volume, velocity, and:
questions.explain: Variety: structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data.

questions.prompt: Velocity, in big data, means:
choices: How fast data arrive, from batches to live streams
How many kinds of data there are
questions.explain: GPS traces and sensor feeds are high-velocity.

questions.prompt: Which source is usually the most authoritative?
choices: A government agency, such as the Census Bureau
questions.explain: Federal, state, county, and local government data are usually most authoritative.

questions.prompt: A dataset that is a fixed snapshot, never updated, is:
questions.explain: Dynamic data keep updating, so results can change when you rerun your code.

questions.prompt: Rerunning the same code on the same data and getting the same results is called:
questions.explain: Replicability is a new study with new data getting consistent results.

questions.prompt: A new study, using different data to answer the same question, gets consistent results. The original finding is:
questions.explain: Reproducible means the same data and code give the same results.

questions.prompt: How does R Markdown help reproducibility?
choices: It keeps data loading, code, results, and write-up in one document anyone can rerun
It removes the need to cite data
It runs faster than R scripts
questions.explain: Knit the file with the data, and you get the same report.

questions.prompt: Relationships that change from place to place are called:
questions.explain: Remote work might matter more for house values near cities than in rural counties.

questions.prompt: Analyzing census tracts instead of counties can change a project's results.
questions.explain: That's the modifiable areal unit problem.

questions.prompt: Which section of a project states the research question?
questions.explain: The research question drives everything else.

questions.prompt: Which is the best research question?
choices: Is the share of residents who work from home related to median house value in NC counties in 2020?
questions.explain: It is specific, names a place and a time, and is answerable.

questions.prompt: A research question must be phrased as a question.
questions.explain: It doesn't have to be, but that often helps.

questions.prompt: The background section should:
choices: Show what earlier research found and how it shapes your question, data, or methods
questions.explain: It shows you've read what came before.

questions.prompt: Which belongs in data and methods?
choices: The source of your data, the code that tidies it, and descriptive maps and statistics
questions.explain: Show your work.

questions.prompt: In which section do you discuss limitations and what you'd do differently?
questions.explain: The conclusion answers the question, or explains why you couldn't.

questions.prompt: Which R function gives the citation for a package, such as tidycensus?
questions.explain: Cite your data and your software.

questions.prompt: Any project that uses spatial data is spatial data science.
questions.explain: You also need spatial analysis: a question with spatial aspects, such as a residual map or a test for spatial autocorrelation.

questions.prompt: Spatial data science combines spatial data, maps and visualizations, and:
questions.explain: Done well, it is also open, reproducible, and replicable.
